Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke on Friday assured the people of the state that he would not disappoint them but would do more during his second term in office. The governor made the disclosure during Jumu’at prayers held at the Osogbo Central Mosque, where activities for his second-term inauguration kicked off. A statement signed by Adeleke’s spokesperson, Olawale Rasheed, stated that the governor was represented by his Deputy Governor, Kola Adewusi. The governor recalled the struggles and battles for the sustenance of democracy in the state and vowed to continue to place the interests of the public at the heart of his administration. Commending Osun people for their steadfastness, perseverance and persistent solidarity during the electioneering period, the governor said, “Osun has become a national model, a symbol for people’s power as the foundation of democracy. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “I won’t disappoint Osun people. I will deliver even more than my first term. I am hopeful our financial situation will soon improve with the expected resolution of the local government crisis. We will take good care of workers and all segments of the society.” Earlier in his sermon, the Deputy Imam of the Osogbo Central Mosque, Sheikh Moruf Ishola, described the recent Osun election as “unprecedented in many respects and a standout record for all students of democracy.” Ishola further said the Osun election that returned Adeleke broke all records in terms of its dynamics and colours, adding that “the August 15 polls defied all calculations because almighty Allah ran it. He must continue to govern with the fear of God, keep promises and serve only the interests of the people.” The prayer session was attended by the Secretary to the State Government, Teslim Igbalaiye; Osun Central Accord senatorial candidate, Ganiyu Olaoluwa; members of the state executive council; special advisers; and top government functionaries. PUNCH Online earlier reported that the Osun State Government had said President Bola Tinubu, governors in the South-West and diplomats had been invited to the second-term inauguration of Adeleke. The Secretary to the State Government, Teslim Igbalaiye, who chairs the inauguration committee, disclosed this while unveiling programmes lined up for the event at a press conference in Osogbo. Igbalaiye said the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, several federal lawmakers, and the governor’s friends and associates from across the world had also been invited to the inauguration, scheduled to hold at the Osogbo Township Stadium on November 27.
